comparisons.peer_summary: Card income increased, reflecting higher net interchange on increased debit and credit card sales volume, as well as higher annual fees in CCB, partially offset by an increase in amortization related to new account origination costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and JPMorgan (JPM) report an increase in card income for 2024, but they attribute the growth to different primary drivers. BAC cites an increase of $230 million driven by higher late fees, annual fees, and card transfer fees. In contrast, JPM attributes its card income increase to higher net interchange resulting from increased debit and credit card sales volume, as well as higher annual fees, partially offset by increased amortization of new account origination costs. While both mention annual fees as a contributing factor, BAC emphasizes fee-based revenues (late, transfer) while JPM emphasizes volume-driven interchange and cost amortization.
